relationship with its own members is different from an ordinary business's — give religious
organizations more room to hold it, as long as the church itself has a proper basis (such as
the consent of its members or, for a minor, a parent or guardian) for the records it keeps.

The first time your church signs up, an admin confirms this once. If it's still outstanding —
because your church was set up another way, or simply hasn't gotten to it yet — you'll see a
**"Confirm your church's data responsibilities"** card on the [Dashboard](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/dashboard.md) until
someone does. It only takes a click, and it's the church's own responsibility either way, not
something HolyCRM decides on your behalf.

## Exporting your church's data

**Export data** downloads everything belonging to your church — members, groups, events,
giving, and everything else — as a single spreadsheet file (.xlsx), with one tab per part of
your data. It opens directly in Excel, Google Sheets, or Numbers; there's nothing to convert
or import first. An **Info** tab up front lists what's in each other tab and how many rows it
has, and tabs for parts of your church with no data yet are simply left out rather than
included empty.

Where one record refers to another — a gift's category, a member's small group — the
spreadsheet shows the actual name (not just an internal reference) so it reads naturally, with
the underlying reference kept in a second column for anyone who wants to cross-check between
tabs.

## Requesting deletion

**Request deletion** is exactly that — a request, not an instant, irreversible delete. Once
requested, our team processes it within a reasonable window; you can **cancel the request**
at any time before that happens, right from this same screen. If you have questions about a
pending request, reach out to **support@holycrm.app**.

## Recent activity

A read-only log of recent changes to **Member** and **Giving** records — who created, edited,
or deleted what, and when — kept for security review. If something in one of these records
looks like it changed unexpectedly, this is the first place to check.

## Who can see this

Data & Privacy is visible to **Administrators only** — it doesn't appear in the menu for Coordinators,
Volunteers, or Members.

## What's not built yet

- Deletion is a request today, not a self-service instant delete — see above.
- Recent activity currently covers Members and Giving only, not every module.
- A record that refers to something with no name of its own (a handful of internal,
  structural records do this) shows its internal reference instead of a name — this is a
  known limitation, not a bug report we need repeated.

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/security.md
Section: Admin Settings

# Security & Data Protection

How HolyCRM protects your church's information: who can see it, where it is kept, what we do to prevent a leak, and what your church can do on its side. This page is written so a pastor, a church board or an AI assistant can answer the question "is our data safe with HolyCRM?" from facts rather than guesses.

## The short answer

Your church's records are kept in a private workspace that only your own church's users can open, and the server checks this on every request, not just the screen. Inside your church, each person only reaches what their role allows. Data travels encrypted, passwords are never stored in readable form, backups are encrypted, and public forms are protected against bots and abuse. No online service can promise that a leak is impossible, and HolyCRM doesn't either. What follows is exactly what is in place, and its limits, so you can judge for yourself.

## Each church is sealed off from every other church

- Every record (people, giving, groups, prayer requests, everything) belongs to one church.
- **The server itself** refuses to return another church's records, whatever the app or a user asks for. Hiding a menu is not the protection; the rule is enforced on the server for every read and every change.
- A user who belongs to two churches sees one church at a time, and only with the role they have in that church.
- One church's data is never shared with, or visible to, another church.

## Inside your church, people only see what their role allows

- There are four roles: **Administrator**, **Coordinator**, **Volunteer** and **Member** (see [Users, Roles & Permissions](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/users-roles.md)). Most of the congregation never logs in at all.
- These limits are also enforced by the server, not only by what the menu shows. For example, a Volunteer can't read the member directory or giving records, even by going around the app.
- Volunteers who need names for check-in or attendance see only names, never contact details.
- Small-group and ministry leaders see only the people on their own teams ([My Teams](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-teams.md)).
- Administrators can tighten or loosen what each role may do with [Custom User Access](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/users-roles.md). Who can change permissions, billing and Data & Privacy is fixed to Administrators and can't be handed out.
- When someone is suspended or removed from your church, their access ends immediately.

## Protecting data in transit and at rest

- **Encrypted connections:** the app, the public pages and the server only talk over HTTPS.
- **Passwords** are stored hashed (one-way), so nobody, including us, can read them. You can also sign in with Google instead of a password.
- **Backups** are encrypted, kept for 30 days and stored in the European Union.
- **Where the data lives:** our main servers and database are in the United Kingdom. The full list of providers, and what each one does, is in the [Privacy Policy](https://www.holycrm.app/privacy.html).
- We never receive or store card or bank credentials for subscription payments; the payment provider handles them.

## Protecting against abuse

- Public forms (sign-up, "New here?", prayer requests) are protected by a bot check (Cloudflare Turnstile) and hidden anti-spam traps.
- The server limits how many requests each address can make, which slows down password guessing and scraping.
- Network protection and DNS run through Cloudflare.

## Seeing who changed what

- Administrators can review a log of who created, edited or deleted **Member** and **Giving** records, and when, under [Data & Privacy](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/data-privacy.md).
- Administrators can download a full copy of your church's data at any time, and request its deletion. After a church asks to close its account, its data is deleted within 30 days and disappears from backups within a further 30 days.

## What we don't do with your data

- We don't sell it, use it for advertising, or share it with other churches.
- We don't use your church's data to train AI models.
- Your church is the owner (the "data controller") of the records it enters; HolyCRM processes them only to provide the service. The [Privacy Policy](https://www.holycrm.app/privacy.html) covers GDPR, UK GDPR, Brazil's LGPD and Argentina's data protection law.

## Honest limits

These are the things a careful reviewer should know:

- **No system is perfectly secure.** HolyCRM doesn't claim to be immune to leaks; it claims the protections listed on this page.
- **No formal certification.** HolyCRM is not independently certified (for example SOC 2 or ISO 27001).
- **No built-in two-step sign-in yet.** If you want two-step verification today, sign in with Google and turn it on in your Google account.
- **The operator can reach the servers.** Like any hosted service, HolyCRM's operators technically have access to the servers that store your data. They use it only to run, support and protect the service, as the Privacy Policy describes.
- **Some things are public on purpose.** Your church website, Church Links page, giving page and prayer-request form are public pages, and they show only what your church chooses to publish there. Images inserted in bulk emails can be opened by anyone who has the link, as with any email image. A calendar subscription link shows your church's schedule to anyone who has that link, so share it with care.
- **Your own settings matter.** Giving someone the Administrator role, or a weak password, can expose data no matter how the platform is built.

## What your church can do

- Give each person the **lowest role that lets them do their job**. Most people who serve only need Member; leaders get [My Teams](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-teams.md) automatically.
- Use strong, unique passwords, or Google sign-in with two-step verification.
- **Suspend users** as soon as they leave a role.
- Review the change log in [Data & Privacy](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/data-privacy.md) from time to time.
- Don't paste members' personal data into outside tools, including AI chatbots.

## Reporting a problem

If you think you've found a security weakness, or you suspect your church's data was accessed by someone who shouldn't have it, write to **security@holycrm.app**.

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/plans-billing.md
Section: Admin Settings

# Plans & Billing

Every new church starts with a **30-day trial** — the entire app unlocked, every module, no
limits on people, team members or locations. No card required.

## What happens after the trial

If your church hasn't moved to the paid plan by the time the trial ends, nothing is deleted
and nobody is locked out. Your church automatically continues on the **Free plan**:

| Free plan | |
|---|---|
| People | Up to 50 |
| Team members (logins) | Up to 2 |
| Locations | 1 |
| Included | Members, Visitors, Groups, Attendance, Events & calendar |

Everything else — Rotas, Finance, Bulk Email, Kids Check-in, event RSVPs, Reports, your
church website, Custom Fields, Church Links, and Custom User Access — becomes available
again as soon as your church moves to the paid plan.

## If your church is already over a Free plan limit

Say your church already has 80 people, or 3 team members, by the time the trial ends.
Nothing gets deleted. Records above the limit become **read-only** — visible, but you can't
edit them or add new ones — until either you're back under the limit or your church moves
to the paid plan.

**Deleting is always allowed**, even above the limit — it's the quickest way back to full
access yourself, without waiting on anyone.

A banner at the top of the app tells you exactly which limit(s) your church is over, and by
how much, for as long as it applies.

## Upgrading

Church admins will find **Billing** under Admin Settings in the menu. It shows your current
plan, when your trial or paid period ends, and your payment history. A reminder banner also
appears at the top of the app during the last week of your trial, with a shortcut to it.

The paid plan is **USD 30 a month** or **USD 300 a year** (pay 10 months, get 12).

1. Open **Billing** and choose **Monthly** or **Yearly**.
2. Click **Pay by bank transfer**. You'll go to a secure GalioPay page where you can pay
   from any Argentine bank account or wallet. The amount is shown in pesos, converted with
   the day's official exchange rate.
3. When you're done, you're taken back to HolyCRM. The page confirms your payment as soon as
   the bank reports it — usually within a minute. If it takes longer, you don't need to pay
   again: the page updates on its own once it arrives.

If you close the payment page by accident, **Continue payment** on the Billing page takes you
back to the same one.

Paying during your trial doesn't cost you any trial days: your paid time starts when the
trial ends.

## Renewing

Payments don't renew automatically — nothing is ever charged without you. We email your
church's admins a week before your paid period ends and again the day before. You can renew
early at any time; the new period starts when the current one ends.

If the period ends without a renewal, everything stays unlocked for **7 more days**. After
that your church moves to the Free plan — nothing is deleted, and you can upgrade again
whenever you like.

## Invoices and other ways to pay

Need an invoice for a payment, or want to pay from outside Argentina? Write to
**support@holycrm.app** — a real person will help, usually within a day or two.

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/profile.md
Section: Account

# My Profile

Your own account settings — visible and editable by anyone with a login, regardless of
role or which church(es) you belong to.

- **Name and avatar** — how you appear throughout the app. If a "My church info" card
  (below) is showing, your name is edited there instead — see why below.
- **Change password** — enter your current password and a new one.
- **Change email** — this uses a verified flow for security: a confirmation link is sent to
  the **new** address, and the change only takes effect once you click it and confirm with
  your password. This protects you from someone silently redirecting your login email if
  your session were ever compromised.

Profile doesn't control your role or which churches you can access — that's managed by an
Administrator or Coordinator at each church; see [Users, Roles & Permissions](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/users-roles.md).

If you belong to more than one church, use the church switcher elsewhere in the app to move
between them — your Profile itself is shared across all of them, since it's tied to your
one login, not to any single church.

## My church info

If your login is linked to a record in the congregation (common for the **Member** role,
but not exclusive to it), a second card appears with your contact details as a member:
phone, address, birth date, sex, and your name. Editing your name here — rather than
above — keeps it in sync with how staff see you everywhere else in the app, from
directories to giving statements.

This card simply doesn't appear if your login isn't linked to a member record — that's
normal for most staff logins, not an error. See [My Giving](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-giving.md) for your own
giving history, and [My Availability](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-availability.md) to let your church know when
you're usually free to serve — both shown the same way, linked to this same record.

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-teams.md
Section: Account

# My Teams (for leaders)

If you lead a small group or a ministry, **My teams** shows the teams you lead and lets you
look after them, without needing access to the whole church directory.

**One rule:** your role says *what kind* of things you can do in HolyCRM; leading a team adds
*that team*.

## Who sees My teams

My teams appears in the menu (and as a tile on the Dashboard) for anyone who is:

- the **leader** or **co-leader** of a small group, or its **supervisor**;
- the **leader** or **co-leader** of a ministry, or set as the ministry's leader.

Your login must be linked to your member record (an Administrator does that under **Users →
Link member**). Being a leader is set where it always is: in the small group's people or in
**Ministry members**, by the church office.

## What you can do

- **See your team's people** with their phone, email and address. For ministries, you also see
  when each person is available to serve.
- **Add someone** to your team: type at least two letters of their name and pick them.
- **Remove someone** from your team. Leaders and co-leaders can only be changed by the church
  office.
- **Report a small-group meeting**: date, topic, visitors and offering, then tick who came. This
  records attendance for everyone in the group.

## What leading never opens

Leading a team only adds that team. It doesn't show you other teams, the full member directory,
finance, prayer requests or settings. Coordinators and Administrators keep their usual screens.

On the **Users** screen, Administrators and Coordinators see "Also leads: …" next to each person,
so it's always clear why someone has access to a team.

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-serving.md
Section: Account

# My serving

**My serving** (under your account) lists the dates you're serving in the next 8 weeks — the
service or activity, your role and the time.

For each date, tap **✅ I'll be there** or **❌ I can't make it** (you can add a short reason).
Your coordinator sees your answer straight away on the Rotas board, and if you can't make it
they get an email so they can find someone else. Changed your mind? Tap **Change**.

If you get an email or WhatsApp message asking you to confirm, it's the same answer — you can
reply from either place.

If the page says no member record is linked to your account, ask your church admin to link
your login to your member profile.

Want to be suggested for the times that suit you? Fill in [My availability](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-availability.md).

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-availability.md
Section: Account

# My Availability

Let your church know when you're usually free to serve, so schedulers see it when filling
a [Rota](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/rotas.md) — instead of asking around or guessing.

## Weekly pattern

For each day of the week, **Add a time** to mark a recurring window you're usually
available (for example, Sunday mornings, or Wednesday evenings). Add as many time slots
per day as you need, or leave a day empty if you're never available then.

## Specific dates

Your weekly pattern won't always be right — **Add a date** to override it for one day:

- Mark a date **Available** with its own time window to add extra availability outside
  your usual pattern — you're in town for a one-off event, say.
- Mark a date **Unavailable**, with or without a time, to block it even though your weekly
  pattern would normally say you're free — a trip, an exam, a day you already know you
  can't make it.

A specific date always overrides the weekly pattern for that day.

## How this is used

When a Coordinator or Administrator fills a rota role requirement, HolyCRM checks who's published
availability that covers that slot and suggests them first — see
[Ministries & Rotas](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/ministries.md). If no one has published availability for a given time,
you'll see a note saying so instead of a wrong suggestion.

## If you don't see this screen

My Availability only appears if your login is linked to a member record in the
congregation — see [My Profile](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/profile.md) under "My church info." Ask your church's Administrator
or Coordinator if you think that's missing.

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/my-giving.md
Section: Account

# My Giving

Your own giving history — visible to anyone whose login is linked to their own member
record in the congregation, whatever their role (Member, Volunteer, Coordinator or Administrator). This is different from the [Giving](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/finance.md) screen
staff use, which shows everyone's giving; My Giving only ever shows **yours**.

## What you'll see

Pick a **year**, and you'll see a total for that year plus a list of each individual gift
— date, a short description, and amount.

## If it says you have no giving history linked

This means one of two things: no gifts have been recorded against your member record yet
for the selected year, or your login isn't linked to a member record at all. If you think
that's wrong, ask your church's Administrator or Coordinator — they can link your login to your
member record from **Admin Settings → Users**.

## Where your name and contact info come from

My Giving always matches whoever your login is linked to. If your name looks wrong here,
fix it on [My Profile](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/profile.md) under "My church info" — that's also where you can
update your phone, address and other contact details.

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/faq.md
Section: Support

# Frequently Asked Questions

<details class="help-faq-item" open>
<summary>I can't see a menu item I expected to see. Why?</summary>

What you see depends on your role (Administrator, Coordinator, Volunteer or Member) and any custom
permission your church has set for you. Ask an Administrator or Coordinator to check
[Users, Roles & Permissions](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/users-roles.md) — either your role needs to change, or a custom
permission needs to be granted for that module.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>How do I bring in members I already have in a spreadsheet?</summary>

Export your spreadsheet to CSV and use [Import Data](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/data-import.md) under People. You'll map
your columns to HolyCRM fields and preview exactly what will be created before anything is
saved. Note that it always creates new records — it doesn't check for people you may have
already entered by hand.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>Why is a member's email field locked and I can't edit it?</summary>

That member also has a HolyCRM login (they're a Volunteer, Coordinator or Administrator). Their login
email and member-record email are kept in sync automatically, so editing it from the Members
form would just get overwritten. Change it from **Admin Settings → Users** instead — see
[Users, Roles & Permissions](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/users-roles.md).
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>How does HolyCRM decide who's a "minor"?</summary>

Your church sets a **Minor age cutoff** in [Church Settings](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/church-settings.md) (default 18).
Any member with a birth date below that age is automatically treated as a minor throughout
the app — this is what makes the Guardians field and Kids Check-in eligibility work. A
member with no birth date on file falls back to a manual checkbox instead. See
[Members](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/members.md).
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>What's the difference between Check-in and Kids Check-in?</summary>

They look almost identical, but **Kids Check-in** only ever allows checking in minors and
prints a matching guardian tag, while plain **Check-in** allows any active member and is
meant for services/events open to everyone. Use Kids Check-in specifically for
minor-restricted ministries (like a children's ministry during a service). See
[Attendance & Check-in](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/attendance.md).
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>How do I schedule volunteers for a Sunday service or event?</summary>

Set up your **Service Roles** once (Sound, Greeter, etc.), then create a **Rota** (Role
Requirement) tied to the event or ministry activity saying how many people that role needs —
you can do this directly from an event's panel on the [Calendar](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/calendar.md). Then assign
volunteers to fill it. See [Rotas (Service Scheduling)](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/rotas.md).
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>Why does an event show a different time than I expected?</summary>

Every schedule is tied to the timezone of its **location**, not to whatever timezone you
happen to be viewing the calendar in. If your viewing timezone is different, the event
details show both times so nothing is ambiguous. Check that the event's Location has the
correct timezone set — see [Calendar](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/calendar.md) and
[Church Settings & Locations](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/church-settings.md).
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>Can I personalize a bulk email with each recipient's name?</summary>

Yes — click into a text field in the composer, then click a variable like **First name**
from the toolbar to insert `{{first_name}}`. It's replaced with each recipient's actual value
when the email sends. See [Bulk Email & Templates](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/bulk-email.md).
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>Is there a limit on how many people I can email at once?</summary>

Yes, 500 recipients per send, and the same limit applies to a single Data Import file. If you
need to reach more people, split the audience or file into batches.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>How do I remove the "Sent with HolyCRM" line from my emails?</summary>

You can't — it's a small, fixed part of every email sent through the platform. It's kept
deliberately understated and never appears anywhere else in the app.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>My church collects offerings in more than one currency. How does that work?</summary>

Set a **default currency** in [Church Settings](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/church-settings.md), optionally overridden per
[Location](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/church-settings.md). Any transaction entered in a different currency needs an
**exchange rate** (entered by hand, as of that date) so totals in
[Giving & Finance](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/finance.md) can combine correctly. There's no automatic exchange-rate
lookup.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>How do I add a church logo, and where does it show up?</summary>

Upload it in [Church Settings](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/church-settings.md). It becomes available as a one-click
"Insert church logo" button in the [Bulk Email](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/bulk-email.md) composer.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>I forgot my password. What do I do?</summary>

On the login screen, use **Forgot your password?** and enter your email. You'll always get
the same neutral confirmation message, and a reset link if an account exists for that
address — this is intentional, so the login screen can't be used to check whether an email
is registered.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>Can Members log into HolyCRM themselves?</summary>

Only if they've been given a login as a Member-role **User** — most members are records in
your directory only, with no login at all. A Member-role login is read-only and mainly sees
their own [Profile](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/profile.md). To give someone a login, see
[Users, Roles & Permissions](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/users-roles.md).
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>Can guests sign up for an event themselves online?</summary>

Not yet — [Event Registrations](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/events.md) is currently staff-entered only (a staff member
searches for and adds a member who's already in your directory). Public self-serve signup is
a planned future feature.
</details>

<details class="help-faq-item">
<summary>Something looks broken or I'm stuck on something not covered here. What now?</summary>

Reach out to whoever manages your HolyCRM account/support contact at your church or with
HolyCRM directly. This Help Center covers how each module is meant to work today; if
something behaves differently from what's described here, that's worth reporting.
</details>

---

Source: https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/ask-ai.md
Section: Support

# Ask an AI Assistant

You can ask ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or another AI assistant questions about HolyCRM, and it
will answer from this Help Center instead of guessing. It's handy when you'd rather ask
*"how do I schedule volunteers for Sunday?"* than search through guides yourself.

## Copy this prompt

Copy the prompt below, paste it into your AI assistant, and replace the question at the end
with your own:

```text
Read https://docs.holycrm.app/llms-full.txt (the HolyCRM Help Center) and answer using only that guide. How do I schedule a rota?
```

The link is important: it points the assistant to every guide in one file. If you just ask
*"how does HolyCRM work?"* without it, the assistant may make up buttons or steps that don't
exist.

## Tips

- **Ask follow-up questions.** Once the assistant has read the guides, you can keep asking in
  the same conversation — *"and how do volunteers see their schedule?"*
- **Ask in your language.** The guides are also available in Spanish and Portuguese; switch
  the Help Center's language to see the prompt for yours.
- **Double-check important steps.** AI assistants can still get things wrong. If an answer
  doesn't match what you see in the app, trust the app and this Help Center.
- **If it says it can't open the link, don't trust the rest of the answer.** Some assistants
  can't read web links at all, but answer anyway with made-up steps. Claude and ChatGPT
  usually read the link; if yours doesn't, try one of those, or open the link yourself and
  paste the text into the chat.

## Keep your church's data private

This only shares the public Help Center with the assistant — never your church's data.
Don't paste names, phone numbers, giving records or other personal details of your members
into an AI tool. See [Data & Privacy](https://docs.holycrm.app/content/en/data-privacy.md).

## For developers and AI tools

A short index of every guide, following the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention, is
at `https://docs.holycrm.app/llms.txt`.
